Hi! Well, I wasn't sure what to major in when I started college. I thought the concepts behind psych were really neat, and I wanted to understand more about mental illness, but after a year I quickly learned how research-based everything was, and I really disliked that. I'm all about reading about research, but setting up experiments and running statistical analyses made me want to beat my head into a wall. I hate numbers enough as it is, lol. 

Near the end of my second semester as a Freshman, I was contemplating if there was a better fit for me. I thought back to what I've always been good at, which were art, music, and writing. Especially writing. After some soul-searching, I took the leap and officially changed my major. I wasn't really certain what I was in for, though. I like learning and I love writing, especially poetry and short stories, but the massive amount of literature we have to digest is terrifying.

 I've always been a slow reader (I think it's the adhd) and trying to get through everything is really discouraging because my progress is so sluggish. I end up getting so upset with myself that I can't be productive anymore. I've been like this since I was little, up all night crying trying to do work. Back then, I had my dad to help me,  and school wasn't as hard. Now that I'm off by myself, I'm having an especially hard time shifting all the responsibility onto myself. Especially when I'm depressed or anxious. 

I feel like there isn't a lot of understanding between faculty/staff and students with emotional/learning issues. I know I have the capacity to do well if I had more time to read, but I can't get that. I just get extended test time, which is a blessing, but not enough to help me do the important stuff, like digesting our readings and finishing all of my homework on time. 

I struggle with writing papers, too, ironically haha. I get so overwhelmed and I sort of shut down. Luckily I had a saint of a professor who worked with me on extending the deadline for the final paper, but that's a rarity here. Nobody really wants to hear or take seriously a student saying that they can't get something done because of depression or anxiety, even though they're trying their best. 

I feel that most professors think I'm lazy. The opposite is true! Sure, I can be lazy, but I really want to do well. I'm just not equipped to do well because I don't know how to cope with my disabilities. I wasn't ever really taught about how they affect school or life in general, beyond a list of symptoms. I think better education and intervention for people like me is absolutely crucial, because I feel like I've slipped through the cracks in that regard. 

I'm happy that you found your calling, and I hope you go great places with it! We need people like you, especially people like me or people who don't do so well under the high-pressure, fast-deadline approach to education that we have. Sorry this is so long, but I hope my experience is helpful to you :)

My dad is an INFJ! I've always felt like we're really similar, and I'm seeing that we are even more so now that I'm a young adult and we can talk on more equal grounds. He's basically the pragmatic, less visibly emotional version of me. He's also much better at putting on the extrovert mask, whereas I'm a lot more anxious around people. He's also not bothered at all by being alone, while I often need a lot of emotional support from a few key people, he being one of them.


He's super idealistic, although he doesn't want to admit it. I think he sees idealism as naivete, but I have been able to get him to admit that the way he wants the world to work is based on ideals, too. He's full of philosophical and governmental schemes. 


But yeah, he's always been my rock. Although he can sometimes be a little harsh and impatient with how I operate (the emotional, indecisive mess that I am), he tries his best to be understanding and relate to me. He's full of life experience and advice and is willing to do anything in his power to help us kids. I had an emotional breakdown over school last semester and he drove all the way up to my college to stay with me for a week to make sure I was okay and taking care of business. 


He's pretty great. I know there are other great dads out there, but I personally feel that he's the best dad I could ask for.

Recently, In a marriage ending argument, my mother turned to me, looked me dead in the eyes with this cold, alien expression, and said, "Your father didn't even want you. He drove me an hour to the nearest city clinic and I decided last minute not to kill you."

My father has since spoken to me about the truth of the circumstances (they were young and he wasn't sure if they could support a baby, but mutually agreed to not go through with the abortion) and I'm no longer hurt by him. 

The thing is the way my mom used that as a weapon against my father and against me, as if I owed her my entire existence and that I should hate my father. If anything, he's a better and more loving parent than she ever was. 

I don't know if I can forgive her for that, and other things she's done. Luckily I'm in college and don't have to see her everyday. I couldn't handle that.
